_comment: Per-package gzipped-size budgets in bytes. Measured against the ESM entry graph: dist/index.js plus every relative file it reaches, gzipped together, so a package that code-splits is still measured on what importing it costs. Tune up explicitly when a primitive batch lands; tune down when a refactor genuinely shrinks output. NOTE on @usemotif/icons: the dist barrel re-exports 1,933 lucide-derived glyphs; the budget reflects the full-barrel size, but real consumers tree-shake to ~100 B gz per imported icon (sideEffects: false guarantees it). Lowered once when lucide's aliases became re-exports of their target glyph instead of duplicate copies of it. NOTE on @usemotif/headless: raised twice while the package moved to a directive-free entry over a client chunk, first by 408 gzipped bytes and then by 356 more as that entry took over assembling all 17 compound namespaces. Both increases are the entry alone; across the second one the client chunk holding the components actually shrank by 146 bytes. Import cost fell at the same time, because a namespace built from plain bindings tree-shakes where an object of components did not: the Dialog-only and Tooltip-only targets in check-tree-shaking.mjs dropped by 14 and 24 percent. NOTE on @usemotif/react, @usemotif/reset and @usemotif/migrate: these emit shared chunks alongside their entry, so their budgets were raised once to cover the whole graph rather than the entry fragment they used to be compared against.
